entities.summary: Allahverdi Khan was a Safavid general and statesman of Georgian origin who, initially a gholām, rose to high office in the Safavid state. Born into a noble family in the late 16th century, Khan's early life was marked by his loyalty to the Safavid Empire, which stretched from modern-day Iran to parts of Turkey and Central Asia. He played a key role in the empire's military campaigns, including the Siege of Baghdad in 1623, which resulted in the city's capture and the subsequent transfer of power to the Safavid dynasty. Khan's leadership and strategic thinking earned him a place among the Safavid elite, and he served as a governor in several provinces, including Georgia and Azerbaijan. His legacy extended beyond his military achievements, as he also played a significant role in the development of the Safavid administrative system, which emphasized decentralization and local autonomy. Khan's impact on the region was cemented by his involvement in the Treaty of Erzurum in 1623, which marked a significant turning point in the history of the Safavid Empire. Despite his importance, Khan's life was cut short when he died on May 24, 1614, at the age of around 40. Today, he is remembered as a pivotal figure in the history of the Safavid Empire, whose legacy continues to shape the cultural, political, and economic landscape of the region.
